items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: and we were wonderful friends, and I lean towards

ctx.x: Zutty and I were close and dear friends. I knew him from 1936 until his death in the '70's, which his work rubbed off on me and it influenced my work in that particular era, and it was especially predominant in the Artie Shaw record which was Blues A and Blues B, a collector's item now -- it was double sided, 78, and I think it was a Columbia recording, but I'm not sure. But I think you will hear all of their influences in my playing on these sides -- at that time, before I had changed to what was my present day…

George Wettling, another great Chicago drummer, with superb taste, he got a musical sound in tuning his drums, he was well studied in drum instruction, and a most exciting soloist -- his solos also had a great deal of humor in them, technique -- and we were wonderful friends, and I lean towards

many of his musical approaches as my own career continued. George and I first knew, after I followed him in Shaw's first big band, and I would find him at Nick's in the Village, in 1936, and he was with Bunny Berigan's first band, and one-nighters through New England, we had battles of music with them, and a battle of music in those days was two bands that was promoted by the ballroom, and the bookers, two bands in the same ballroom taking alternative sets, and let the people decide which band they liked best.
